reads: a parse of the Bash command

cases.name: deny-plain-push
cases.why: Every form of git push is denied; the door does not judge the push, it moves it to the script.

cases.name: deny-push-with-pinned-lease
cases.why: A pinned lease is still a push, and this door is about where a push is run from rather than whether it is safe: a rewritten branch goes through scripts/publish.sh --rebased.

cases.name: deny-push-refspec
cases.why: The safest spelling of a push is still a push.

cases.name: deny-push-delete
cases.why: A deletion is a push, and the script has a mode for it that checks the ref existed and is gone.

cases.name: deny-push-after-a-wrapper
cases.command: sudo -u ncenter git push origin main
cases.why: Wrappers are stripped before the command is read, as they are for every other rule.

cases.name: deny-push-with-git-global-options
cases.why: The subcommand is found past git's own options.

cases.name: deny-push-second-in-a-chain
cases.command: git status --short && git push origin main
cases.why: Every simple command is read, not only the first.

cases.name: deny-push-inside-a-live-heredoc
cases.why: An unquoted heredoc's substitution really runs, so the push is real.

cases.name: allow-the-publish-script
cases.why: The script is the way through the door. Its own push is a child process and never reaches a PreToolUse hook.

cases.name: allow-push-in-quoted-text
cases.why: A quoted string is text; the command is echo.

cases.name: allow-push-in-a-quoted-heredoc
cases.command:
cat <<'EOF' > notes.md
git push origin main
EOF
cases.why: A quoted delimiter makes the body inert, so nothing runs.

cases.name: allow-push-in-a-commit-message
cases.command: git commit -m "do not git push by hand"
cases.why: The word push appears in an argument, not as a subcommand.

cases.name: allow-git-log-mentioning-push
cases.why: A different subcommand that merely names this one.

cases.name: allow-push-like-subcommand
cases.why: The subcommand is compared whole, so a longer name is a different command.

cases.name: allow-ls-remote
cases.why: Asking the server what it holds is not writing to it, and the script does exactly this afterwards.

cases.name: allow-unparseable-command
cases.why: A parse that will not resolve allows, like every other rule here -- and the door is no exception, however important it is.

cases.name: deny-push-to-a-build-clone-ci-ref
cases.why: A push to another clone's refs/ci is a push like any other. A lane's commit reaches its build worktree through scripts/compute-host.py sync, whose push is a child process this never sees.
